reason: Wrong about the code, wrong about the sentence, and the fix would import a defect this panel has already paid to remove. (1) Wrong about the binding. render-b.js:1243 reads window.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll, {passive:true}) FIRST, and the pane listener is the conditional second add; the edge accessor already branches - edge = pane && overflowY==="auto" ? pane.top : 0 - i.e. it is written to run with the window as the scroller. The mechanism is not 'wired only to the owner's pane scroller'. What is true is narrower: the whole block sits inside wireOwner(), and states.desk never calls it. (2) Wrong that the sentence goes stale. Driven at 1440, 1280 and 1152 with state=desk: .b-stick is sticky top:40px, the window is the scroller, max scroll is 733px at 1440 / 793 at 1280 / 893 at 1152 - LESS THAN ONE SCREENFUL on a 1693px document. At the bottom the pinned column reads MARA & FINN / 79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day / TODAY IS 16 JULY / Nothing is planned until 1 August. Every line of that is true at every scroll position. It is a masthead of invariants - who, the day, the count to the day, now, and when the plan starts - and nothing in it claims to describe the rows beside it. 'Nothing is planned until 1 August' is a fact about the stretch from today to the first moment, not a viewport readout; it is the second half of the thought that begins 'Today is 16 July', which is why the two sit under one rule with 450px of empty column beneath them. The screenshot at max scroll shows no contradiction: 1 August is 349px above the fold, and 29 August through 3 October - the wedding day itself - are all on screen. The finding's own figures are off too: it drives 1200px where the window stops at 733, and 'the guest scrolls to October' overstates a page that ends with the whole back half still visible. (3) The fix would make it worse, in the way already refuted. Simulating the owner rule with edge=0 on this state: at max scroll the line becomes '29 August · 44 days away' (1440), '5 September · 51 days away' (1280), '19 September · 65 days away' (1152) - a restatement of the topmost row 350px to its right, printed directly under 'Today is 16 July' and directly under a 79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 block. That is the 'prints the same fact three times within 250px' objection the round notes record as settled, and it permanently deletes the only statement of when the plan begins from a document the reader scrolls once and never scrolls back - the unanchored-time defect a prior round already paid for. The owner/guest asymmetry is earned, not an oversight: the owner's desk is a fixed frame whose plan is a pane that can scroll arbitrarily far under an unmoving HUD while they edit, so a HUD that never updates is genuinely stale; the guest's desk is one document scrolling as a unit under a sticky title card, and a received keepsake whose title card rewrites its own sentences under the reader's thumb reads as telemetry, not as something a person sent. interaction-check.mjs states the same reading in its own comment at the pinned-column assertion. Round 8 did not break the guest surface; it built a scroll readout for the one surface that needed one.
